title: The Blue Door
author: Tadoku Note (original)
summary: 引っ越した先の家には、鍵のかかった青いドアがありました。ドアの向こうから、夜になると音が聞こえます。

source.note: Original text written for this app.

paragraphs: Mia and her parents have a new house. It is old and big. It has a red kitchen, a green living room and a long dark hall.
At the end of the hall, there is a blue door. Mia tries to open it. She cannot. It is locked.
“Dad, what is behind the blue door?” she asks.
“I don’t know,” her father says. “We don’t have a key for it. Maybe it is a closet.”
That night, Mia is in bed. The house is quiet. Then she hears a sound. Tap. Tap. Tap. It comes from the hall.
Mia gets up and goes into the hall. It is very dark. The sound is behind the blue door. Tap. Tap. Tap. Mia is afraid. She runs back to bed.
The next morning, she tells her mother. Her mother laughs. “Old houses make sounds, Mia. It is the wind.”
But the next night, Mia hears it again. Tap. Tap. Tap. And then a new sound. Scratch, scratch. It is not the wind.

On Saturday, Mia looks for the key. She looks in the kitchen. She looks in the garden. She looks under the stairs. There is a small box under the stairs. In the box, there is an old photo and a small blue key.
In the photo, there is a girl with a bird in her hands. On the back of the photo, someone wrote: “Anna and Pip, 1985.”
Mia takes the key to the blue door. Her hands are cold. She puts the key in the door. It turns. The door opens.

Behind the door, there are stairs. They go up. Mia goes up the stairs slowly. At the top, there is a small room with a round window. The window is broken. The room is full of old books, and there are leaves on the floor.
Tap. Tap. Tap. Mia looks up. There is a bird at the window! It is a small brown bird. It is hitting the glass with its beak. And in the corner of the room, there is a nest.
In the nest, there are three baby birds. Scratch, scratch. They are moving in the leaves. They are hungry.
Mia smiles. “So you are the sound,” she says.
She does not close the window. She does not move the nest. She goes down the stairs very quietly and tells her parents.
Every day after that, Mia goes up to the little room. She sits and reads the old books. She watches the birds. After three weeks, the baby birds fly away.
Now the room is Mia’s room. She puts the photo of Anna and Pip on the wall. And the blue door is never locked again.
